title: CYBRIK Suite W2-F internal service-delegation + workload-identity contract packet — compatibility/version manifest
description: Inventory and compatibility record for the W2-F cross-service identity + application-delegation contract packet (internal SOC → Cyber AI seam). ADDITIVE to, and DISJOINT from, the accepted v0.1 cross-product packet and the ACCEPTED W2-D inference packet: it introduces the cybrik.svc-* JSON Schema namespace and REUSES accepted primitives (common-defs, data-marking) by $ref without modifying them. It realizes the two-layer trust seam of ADR-0006 (E2 mTLS workload identity, E3 delegation) as detailed in ADR-0008. Every member here is ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION at v0.1.0 (not stable v1/GA) as of Gate W2-F (Codex under Founder delegation, 2026-07-24); products MAY now implement contract-first against v0.1.0. This is an implementation-authorization acceptance only — NOT a stable v1/GA promotion and NOT an ADR-0001 immutable bundle tag. $id uses the RFC 2606 .example documentation domain; it is an identifier, not an endpoint.
wire_scope: NO SERVER / NO ENDPOINT. This packet declares no OpenAPI server, AsyncAPI channel, host, route, or operational URL. It is a set of JSON Schema validation contracts (token / request-validation / trust-metadata) plus a mapping note. The seam it governs is realized by each product's own transport (mTLS) and mint/validate code, contract-first against these schemas.
mcp_scope: OUT OF SCOPE. This packet defines no MCP server/tool/action contract and grants no tool/function/agent authority. A delegation token authorizes a named AI inference/summarization operation only; tool execution remains governed by the accepted Tool-Fabric packet (ADR-0004).

adr_basis.role: versioning/format-pin policy (D1, D4, D5, D6); this packet stays v0.1.0 ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION (not stable v1/GA) and is never a bundle tag.

workload identity (E2) + delegation (E3): the two-layer trust seam. Transport = mTLS workload identity; application = short-lived certificate-bound delegation token. This packet is the contract realization of that accepted seam.

internal service-delegation + workload-identity profile: two-layer mTLS (SPIFFE-compatible, not required) + asymmetric RFC 9068 delegation token (<=120s, cnf-bound, strict iss/aud/jti/time), SOC mint port, Cyber AI validate/re-authorize, A05 external boundary kept distinct. This packet is that ADR's contract realization.

adr_out_of_scope.reason: Tool execution authority / capability registry / approval / the digest-bound cybrik.delegation-chain.v1 tool-grant — a SEPARATE accepted packet. This packet's application-delegation token is DISJOINT from that tool-grant chain: it may reference one (cybrik.delegation_ref) but never substitutes for it and grants no tool/action authority.

Org-hierarchy contract delta is PROPOSED — NOT APPLIED. org_scope here is opaque/advisory only and carries no authority; the A05 external-authority boundary (ADR-0007 OD-3) is kept a distinct trust context — its identities are never accepted at this internal seam.
Durable agent orchestration / bus choice — NOT decided here; this packet declares no servers, channels, or bindings.

reuses_accepted_unmodified.note: These accepted v0.1 members are referenced by $ref and are NOT modified, re-versioned, or re-stated by this packet. Backward compatibility of the accepted packet is preserved.

members.title: Service-delegation → W2-D inference operation mapping notes

backward_compatibility.namespace: Disjoint: schema ids cybrik.svc-*. No accepted id, event type, or channel is redefined; the W2-D inference namespace (cybrik.model-*/cybrik.alert-summarization-*) is unchanged and only referenced by neutral operation tokens.
backward_compatibility.relation_to_w2d_inference: This packet governs the IDENTITY/DELEGATION seam in front of the W2-D inference operations. A delegation token authorizes a neutral operation token (e.g. ai.inference.create, ai.summarization.create) that names a W2-D operation WITHOUT importing, modifying, or re-stating any W2-D schema. The two packets are additive and disjoint.

trust_invariants.note: Fail-closed trust invariants. Some are STRUCTURAL (enforced by the JSON Schemas and exercised by fixtures, SI-*); others are RUNTIME-ONLY (the relying party MUST enforce; JSON Schema constrains shape only, SR-*). Both products MUST implement identical outcomes. The transport layer (E2 mTLS) is a deployment obligation; these contracts bind the application layer (E3) to it via cnf.
structural: SI-1 Asymmetric-only signing: header.alg is a jwtAlg (ES*/PS*/RS*/EdDSA); no HS* symmetric and no 'none' is expressible (RFC 8725 §3.1/§3.2; RFC 9068 §4). A delegation token is verified against pinned public JWKS trust, never a shared secret.
SI-2 Explicit typing: header.typ is const 'at+jwt' (RFC 9068 §2.1); a token minted for a different purpose is not accepted as a delegation token.
SI-3 Replay key required: claims.jti is required, minLength 16 — every token carries an unguessable anti-replay id.
SI-4 Sender-constrained: claims.cnf (RFC 8705 x5t#S256, 43-char base64url) is required; a bearer token with no certificate binding, or a malformed thumbprint, is rejected.
SI-5 Complete authorization claim set: iss/sub/aud/iat/nbf/exp and the CYBRIK tenant/actor/operation/marking claims are all required — an under-specified token cannot authorize anything.
SI-6 Single strict audience: aud is a single value (not an array); the relying party matches it exactly to its own identity (confused-deputy defense).
SI-7 No static bearer: the request-validation view is additionalProperties:false — an inline static 'authorization' bearer has nowhere to live.

SI-8 No forwarded end-user token: the request-validation view is additionalProperties:false — an 'on_behalf_of_user_token' cannot be smuggled through; delegation is the RFC 8693 act/actor claim, not a forwarded user credential.
SI-9 Hard short-TTL ceiling: svc-trust-metadata.max_token_ttl_seconds is const 120; require_cnf and require_mtls are const true — the fail-closed defaults are not configurable open.
runtime_only: SR-1 Time window: the relying party MUST reject a token whose nbf is in the future or whose exp is in the past (within a bounded clock_skew_seconds). JSON Schema cannot compare against wall-clock time.
SR-2 Short TTL enforced: the relying party MUST reject a token whose exp - iat exceeds max_token_ttl_seconds (120s) even if currently within its window.
SR-3 Audience match: token.aud MUST equal the relying party's own self_audience; a token for another audience MUST be rejected (RFC 9700 §2.3).
SR-4 Cross-tenant: authoritative tenant is the token's cybrik.tenant_id; a body tenant_id that differs MUST be rejected (advisory body never elevates).
SR-5 Org scope: an advisory body org_scope, when present, MUST match the token's cybrik.org_scope; it carries no authority on its own (ADR-0007 delta not applied).
SR-6 Operation binding: the requested operation.name MUST equal the token's cybrik.operation.name; a body requesting an unauthorized operation MUST be rejected (confused-deputy defense).
SR-7 Marking non-escalation: the request data_marking MUST be at or below the token's cybrik.marking on the classification/TLP lattice; a request above it MUST be rejected.
SR-8 Replay: the relying party MUST reject a second presentation of a jti already seen within its validity window (jti replay cache). Schema cannot track cross-request state.
SR-9 Proof-of-possession: the mTLS peer certificate thumbprint MUST equal token.cnf['x5t#S256']; a token presented without its bound client certificate MUST be rejected (RFC 8705).

SR-10 Issuer/key pinning: iss MUST be in the pinned accepted_issuers set and header.kid MUST resolve to a pinned JWKS key; verification MUST fail closed when trust cannot be resolved (offline/air-gapped included).

cross_ref_integrity.note: Bindings the relying party MUST preserve (schema cannot enforce equality across artifacts / against transport state).
bindings: svc-delegation-token.claims.iss ∈ svc-trust-metadata.accepted_issuers; header.alg ∈ svc-trust-metadata.accepted_algs; (exp - iat) <= svc-trust-metadata.max_token_ttl_seconds

gate.status: DECIDED — ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA)
gate.decided_by: Codex, under explicit Founder delegation of Gate W2-F (not agent-inferred)
decisions_resolved: G-W2F-1 ACCEPTED: the two-layer trust seam — transport mTLS workload identity (SPIFFE-compatible, SPIFFE not required, no SPIRE hard-dependency) + application-layer short-lived asymmetric certificate-bound delegation token — is the internal SOC → Cyber AI cross-service identity contract.

G-W2F-2 ACCEPTED: the delegation token is an RFC 9068 at+jwt, asymmetric-only, <=120s, cnf-bound, with strict iss/aud/jti/time validation and required tenant/org/actor/operation/marking authorization claims.

G-W2F-3 ACCEPTED: SOC mints downstream delegation tokens; Cyber AI validates AND re-authorizes the named operation (never trusts the caller body over the token, nor the token over the mTLS peer certificate).
G-W2F-4 ACCEPTED: the external-authority (A05) boundary is a DISTINCT trust context; internal delegation identities and external identities are never reused across it (ADR-0007 OD-3).
G-W2F-5 ACCEPTED: this packet is disjoint from the Tool-Fabric tool-grant chain (ADR-0004) and from MCP; it maps only to neutral W2-D inference operation tokens with no server/endpoint.
gate.evidence_ref: See acceptance.evidence[] and cybrik-suite:docs/releases/GATE-W2-F-SERVICE-DELEGATION-ACCEPTANCE-2026-07-24.md. A green validator/secret-scan run is a conformance signal; acceptance is the recorded Founder-delegated decision, not an inference from CI.

acceptance.status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION — not stable v1/GA
acceptance.decided_by: Codex, under explicit Founder delegation of Gate W2-F (not agent-inferred)
acceptance.scope: Products MAY now implement against the W2-F service-delegation packet v0.1.0. This is an implementation-authorization acceptance only; it is NOT a stable v1/GA promotion and NOT an ADR-0001 immutable bundle tag. The packet version remains 0.1.0 and x-cybrik-is-bundle-tag remains false. Runtime-only trust invariants (trust_invariants.runtime_only: SR-1..SR-10) and cross_ref_integrity bindings remain explicit and REQUIRED of every implementation; a green validator run proves standards conformance and fixture coverage, not runtime enforcement, and not the presence of an operational CA/mTLS deployment.
evidence: Pinned standards validation green: JSON Schema 2020-12 compile/ref-resolution of the 4 svc schemas (reusing common-defs + data-marking unmodified), 3/3 positive + 7/7 negative-schema + 9/9 negative-semantic fixtures, and the SI-*/SR-* trust-invariant assertions each exercised by a fixture; git diff --check clean; gitleaks secret scan clean (no key material, CA, or secret is a wire field anywhere in the packet).

Independent post-validator security/compatibility review: packet internally coherent at v0.1.0, additive to and disjoint from the accepted v0.1 and W2-D packets, no tool/agent authority, external (A05) boundary kept distinct, and no operational endpoint or CA/secret introduced.
acceptance.mechanics: Acceptance-for-implementation was authorized by explicit Founder delegation of Gate W2-F to Codex and recorded with evidence in this commit (ADR-0001 D5). No approval was inferred from CI going green. Promotion to a stable v1/GA version or an immutable bundle tag remains a separate Founder gate (ADR-0001 D6).
